title: In awake mice, putative LGN-to-V1 spike connections go mostly to fast-spiking layer 4 cells and follow retinotopy weakly, with no consistent ON/OFF rule, in two Allen Neuropixels data sets
abstract: We tested cat and rabbit rules for thalamocortical connections in the awake mouse. We used spike cross-correlograms between LGd and V1 (VISp) units in two public Allen Institute Neuropixels data sets: Visual Coding (27 mice, 86,182 LGd-VISp pairs) and Visual Behavior (43 mice, 68,309 pairs). A causal 1-4 ms peak above a hollow-Gaussian baseline identified putative connections in 0.48% and 0.52% of pairs (LP control: 0.04% and 0.12%). Fast-spiking targets had 1.8% detection versus 0.13-0.24% for regular-spiking targets (odds ratio 7.5 and 4.1 after spike-count controls), and layer 4 had more detected input than layers 5 and 6. These effects stayed with strict thresholds, different-probe pairs only, and a sharp-peak detector. RF-centre distance had a graded effect (odds ratio per 10 degrees 0.85-0.88 with the main detector, 0.71-0.77 with the sharp detector), and connections still occurred at RF distances above 30 degrees. Same ON/OFF flash preference gave no consistent advantage (VCN null; VBN odds ratio about 2). Single connections were weak (median 0.5-0.7% excess spikes per LGN spike onto FS cells). Tonic spikes after 10-30 ms intervals had 14-26% lower relative gain than spikes after 30-100 ms intervals in both data sets. A burst-spike advantage appeared only with the broad baseline. Running did not change the relative gain. Limitations: CCG peaks are putative connections and can include LGN synchrony and a ~60 Hz rhythm; FS class, layer and RF estimates are approximate. Allen data are not bundled; code regenerates all derived tables.

display.caption: Percentage of LGd-VISp pairs with a detected causal 1-4 ms CCG peak, by target class (FS blue, RS orange), target layer, RF-centre distance and flash ON/OFF sign match, in Visual Coding (circles) and Visual Behavior (squares). 95% CI from a bootstrap over mice.

Pooled CCG excess over the hollow-Gaussian baseline for all different-probe pairs (no threshold). LGd input to FS cells in layer 4 gives a causal peak at 1-4 ms (grey band) on top of a ~60 Hz rhythm; RS targets and the LP control show no clear causal peak.
Odds ratios (95% CI, mouse-clustered) of a detected connection for target class, layer, RF distance and ON/OFF sign, across four detection variants and both data sets.
